Subject: Re: sudden spikes in latency + 5xx bursts from redwood SDK

Hi Tessa,

We started seeing a recurring pattern this morning around 08:45 PST where our ingestion path into Redwood shows 10–30s tail latencies and a spike of 502/504 errors for about 12–15 minutes every ~20 minutes. The attached trace (pulse_repro_trace_1107.log) and a packet dump (sdk_packet-dump.txt) come from our staging cluster.

What we observe:
- client SDK appears to retransmit or drop chunks, downstream shows repeated parse failures in the streaming parser, which then surfaces as retries and timeouts from our side.
- error rate up from 0.2% → 6.8% during the window, P95 latency jumped from 180ms → 6.3s.
- impact: our orchestration triggers backpressure and then scales down workers; overall throughput drops ~40%.

This is blocking our end-to-end test runs and is a showstopper for the upcoming pilot go/no-go call next week. Can someone confirm if this is a known client-side parser issue or something on the Redwood transport?

Attached: pulse_repro_trace_1107.log, sdk_packet-dump.txt

Subject: Re: sudden spikes in latency + 5xx bursts from redwood SDK — initial triage

Thanks for the traces — I dug into the packet dump and our server-side logs. Initial analysis:

- Root cause hypothesis: the PulseHealth client (older SDK build) occasionally sends coalesced stream frames where header boundaries and chunk delimiters are merged. Our current streaming parser uses an optimization that attempts to rewind/parse across frames for coalesced payloads. In a narrow edge case (partial header + compression boundary), the parser can enter a short "rewind loop" while trying to resynchronize — CPU per-connection spikes, tokenization stalls, and upstream timeouts follow.

- Why it appears as increased error rate/latency: the rewind loop delays response completion; upstream retry logic increases concurrency and amplifies the CPU spike, producing transient 502/504s and throughput collapse.

- Repro steps (local): 1) run the included packet-dump through our local harness with --simulate-coalesce, 2) set client to SDK v0.9.7 (the last known good is 0.9.12). I reproduced the rewind loop within ~30s.

- Short-term mitigations:
  1) Customer: downgrade to SDK 0.9.12 (patched parser) OR apply server-side chunk alignment (we can do an ingress rewrite rule for PulseHealth traffic).
  2) Ours: hotfix to make parser bail after one rewind attempt and fast-fail to a safe fallback instead of looping.

I'll open a JIRA (JIRA-INC-5123) with a reproducer and a patch candidate within the hour. Maya — if you can run the provided binary build and confirm whether the symptom disappears, that will validate the fix path.

Attachments: repro steps included in JIRA ticket and the packet dump we discussed.
